1#main: The law of cutting a limb of a firstborn and other firstborn laws. In it are 4 seifim. An animal straining to give birth—one may cut it limb by limb and throw to dogs (and from the majority onward it requires burial (Beit Yosef in the name of Tosafot)). And what is born after it is a firstborn (and some say it is not a firstborn (Tur in the name of the Rosh)). If the majority emerged, it is buried and she is released from the firstborn obligation. And if he cut a limb and left a limb until the majority was completed—all the limbs require burial and she is released from the firstborn obligation once the majority emerged, whether whole or cut—and behold it is before us—it was sanctified retroactively. (And some say it is not sanctified retroactively (Tur).)
2#main: If a third emerged and he sold it to a gentile, and another third emerged afterward—it was sanctified retroactively. (And some say it is not sanctified retroactively (Tur).)
3#main: If a third emerged by caesarean and two thirds through the womb—it is not sanctified. (And some say it is sanctified (likewise Tur).)
4#main: If the majority of the fetus emerged through a minority of one of the limbs that completes the majority—it is considered birth even though most of the limb is inside; and it is forbidden to sell it to a gentile and to throw it to dogs, and it releases what is born after it. And if half the fetus emerged through a majority of one limb through which the emergence of half the fetus was completed—behold this is doubtful, and it is forbidden to sell it to a gentile and to throw it to dogs; and what is born after it is a doubtful firstborn.
